result.rootCause:
Category (ordinal) axis ticks are memoized per axis instance, but `Axis#getTicksCoords` never re-checks them against the axis's current scale extent, so when the visible window shrinks (dataZoom narrowing the scale extent on a live axis) the stale ticks are mapped through `dataToCoord` and land outside the axis coord extent / grid rect.

Detail:
1. `src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts:184-224` `makeCategoryTicks` computes ticks from `ordinalScale.getExtent()` and stores them in a per-axis cache keyed only by the tick `interval` option (`getListCache`/`listCacheGet`, lines 244-262). The cache is explicitly assumed to be safe because "axis is created each time during a ec process, so we do not need to clear cache" (comment at lines 241-243). That assumption breaks as soon as the scale extent changes on an existing axis — which is exactly the dataZoom window semantics, and what the requirement's regression test does (`axis.scale.setExtent(2, 4)`).
2. `src/coord/Axis.ts:179-188` maps every returned tick to a coord with no extent test whatsoever. With scale extent [2,4] and cached ticks [0,1,2,3,4] the mapping yields coords -150,-50,50,150,250 for a [0,300] axis.
3. The only clipping in the whole path is inside `fixOnBandTicksCoords` (`src/coord/Axis.ts:291-346`), and it is doubly insufficient:
   - it early-returns for `!axis.onBand || alignWithLabel` (line 296), so `boundaryGap:false` axes and `axisTick.alignWithLabel:true` axes get no clipping at all;
   - its clamp block (`src/coord/Axis.ts:326-337`) removes/rewrites exactly ONE tick per end (`ticksCoords.shift()` / `ticksCoords.pop()`), so when 2+ ticks are out of range the remainder still overflows; and with `clamp:true` it only rewrites `ticksCoords[0].coord = axisExtent[0]`, leaving the second out-of-range tick in place (hence the observed [0,-100,0,...]).
`getMinorTicksCoords` (`src/coord/Axis.ts:199-221`) has no clipping either, but it is not affected: `scale.getMinorTicks()` is always derived from the live extent (verified for Interval and Log, before/after `setExtent`), so no minor-tick overflow was observed.

risks: Do NOT make the filter unconditional (all scale types). The sweep caught a real counterexample: log axis with min/max fixed and filterMode 'none' returns tick value 333333.9999999995 while scale.getExtent()[0] is 333333.99999999953 (pow/round round-trip noise). An unconditional `tickVal >= extent[0]` filter would delete that axis's min tick/splitLine. `round()` (10 decimals) happens to rescue this one case but not large-magnitude values, hence the `scale.type === 'ordinal'` guard.

If the narrowed window happens to contain none of the cached ticks (e.g. axisTick.interval:1 -> cached ticks [0,2,4], window [3,3]), the filtered list is empty, fixOnBandTicksCoords early-returns on `!ticksLen`, and getTicksCoords returns [] even with clamp:true — splitLine/splitArea then draw nothing where today they draw (wrong) lines. If the 'clamp always yields both extent bounds' guarantee must hold, add a guarded `if (clamp && !ticksLen) { return the two axisExtent bounds }` in fixOnBandTicksCoords; note ticks are also legitimately empty when the tick model has show:false, so such a branch must not fire for that case.

Ticks inserted by the clamp branches carry no `tickValue`; consumers already tolerate that (AxisBuilder.ts:645 anid, CartesianAxisView.ts:169-171, axisSplitHelper.ts:71/106-110 all null-check), and dropping out-of-window ticks changes anid identity for those elements, which can only alter axis transition animations, not layout.

The identical staleness exists for labels: getViewLabels() after a scale-extent narrowing still returns the old tickValues (measured coords -150 and -50 for a [0,300] axis), so axis labels would still be drawn outside the grid. The requirement only mentions ticks and the regression test only checks ticks; if label overflow is also in scope, the same filter is needed in createAxisLabels/makeCategoryLabels (or the label cache must be extent-aware).

Grid.ts rebuilds axes on every dataZoom action, so this bug is not visible in the built-in chart pipeline today — the fix is defensive/API-level. Any test that asserts a behavior change at the whole-chart level (dispatchAction + getTicksCoords) will pass both before and after the fix; the meaningful assertions are the Axis-level ones.

correctnessConcerns: SCOPE CHANGE: the diff was revised mid-review. The `_points`/`_stackedOnPoints` release plus the `canDiffPoints` guard described in the review brief (item 4) is NO LONGER PRESENT in the working tree -- it was removed. The current line diff is only (a) turnPointsIntoStep rewritten to exactly-sized Float32Arrays in src/chart/line/LineView.ts, (b) buffer reuse in getStackedOnPoints/getStackedOnPoint (src/chart/line/LineView.ts, src/chart/line/helper.ts), and (c) NEW: optional `out` params added to Polar#dataToPoint and Polar#coordToPoint in src/coord/polar/Polar.ts. Item 4 of the review brief is therefore moot.

LOW / LATENT, NOT DEMONSTRATED: a Float32Array cannot grow, and I confirmed empirically on a live chart that zrender keeps the same array reference for polyline.shape.points and interpolates into it in place (interpolate1DArray writes out[i]; fillArray pads only the plain-array keyframe clone). Step lines now feed Float32Arrays into that path, so if the animation target `next` were ever LONGER than `current`, the tail would be silently dropped where the old plain array would have grown. I traced src/chart/line/lineAnimationDiff.ts and could not construct the case: the '=' branch copies next into current whenever current is NaN, and the '+' branch's oldCoordSys.dataToPoint only yields NaN when the new value is itself NaN (ordinal/log/out-of-extent give finite or +/-Infinity, not NaN), in which case next is NaN too. Non-step lines have always used equal-length Float32Arrays here. Verdict: theoretical robustness note, not a bug.

getStackedOnPoint now passes clamp=false where it previously passed undefined (coordSys.dataToPoint(stackedData, false, out)). Verified equivalent: linearMap, Axis#dataToCoord, dataToRadius and dataToAngle only test truthiness of clamp. Also confirmed empirically on a chart whose yAxis min/max is narrower than the data.

PUBLIC API SURFACE: Polar#dataToPoint(data, clamp?, out?) and Polar#coordToPoint(coord, out?) gain optional params. Grepped every caller (AngleAxisView, PolarAxisPointer, coord/polar/prepareCustom, Polar itself) -- none passes the new argument, so it is backward compatible. Radar#coordToPoint(coord: number, indicatorIndex: number) is a separate class with an unrelated signature and is unaffected. Aliasing contract: when `out` is supplied the return value IS the caller's array; the helper comment documents this and the only caller copies values out immediately.

Buffer reuse is safe: getStackedOnPoint unconditionally assigns both stackedData[0] and stackedData[1] on every call (baseDataOffset and 1-baseDataOffset), so no stale value can leak between data items; Cartesian2D.dataToPoint and Polar.dataToPoint read only data[0]/data[1] and never retain the reference. lineAnimationDiff.ts:127 still calls getStackedOnPoint with no buffers, so it gets fresh arrays.

HARMLESS BEHAVIOR DIFFERENCE in one edge case: when dataCoordInfo.valueDim is falsy, getStackedOnPoints returns []. The old code then produced a length-0 stepped base line; the new code produces a full-length Float32Array of NaN (reading past the empty source). Renders identically -- ECPolygon's drawSegment treats both undefined and NaN as a null point and bails -- and getBoundingDiff yields NaN either way.

PRECISION: only step:'middle' introduces a new float32 rounding (the (base+nextBase)/2 midpoint). start/end turning points are exact copies of values that were already float32 in data.getLayout('points'), so they are bit-identical. Worst-case error is ~1e-4 px at typical canvas sizes, far below drawSegment's own 0.5px tiny-segment threshold. No visual change.

INCOMPLETE OPTIMIZATION (nit): Polar.dataToPoint still allocates the intermediate [radius, angle] array on every call, so a polar area series still allocates one array per data item; the `out` buffer only removes the second allocation. Cartesian2D's applyTransform(out, ...) fast path is fully allocation-free.

QUALITY NITS: `type NumericArray = ReturnType<typeof createFloat32Array>` is indirect -- `number[] | Float32Array` reads better. `writeStepPoints` is a closure re-created on every turnPointsIntoStep call (it captures baseIndex/valueIndex/stepTurnAt); still a net win versus the old toStepPoints closure plus four scratch arrays, but hoisting it would remove the per-call allocation entirely.
result.verdict: PASS -- no correctness defect found. All 380 unit tests pass (68/68 suites), tsc --noEmit and eslint are clean. I verified the new turnPointsIntoStep is bit-for-bit identical to the pre-change HEAD~ algorithm (after float32 quantization of the reference) across 113 configurations covering all three step types, connectNulls on/off, x-base and y-base axes, and 9 null/degenerate datasets including single-point, single-null and zero-point inputs. The step count formula is correct (n>=1 -> 2n-1, middle -> 3n-2; n=0 -> 0, matching the original's `if (rawPoints.length >= 2)` guard), connectNulls filtering is unchanged, NaN is preserved through Float32Array so non-connectNulls gaps still render, and the stepped-line-area-nulls requirement (3e53abe) is not regressed -- step.test.ts is green and stackedOnPoints stayed index-aligned with points in every case. The rewrite is structurally stronger than what it replaces: both arrays are written from the same outOffset driven solely by points' NaN-ness, so the #20092 skew is unrepresentable. Float32Array is safe for every consumer (poly.ts buildPath/drawSegment/getPointOn, isPointsSame, bboxFromPoints, getIndexRange, getPointAtIndex all only index and read .length; no .push/.slice/.concat on shape.points anywhere in src/; lineAnimationDiff already produced Float32Arrays; the no-TypedArray Array fallback leaves no holes because outOffset advances to exactly stepPointCount*2). Two caveats for the author: (1) the _points/_stackedOnPoints release logic named in the review brief is no longer in the diff, and (2) the diff now also widens the public Polar#dataToPoint / Polar#coordToPoint signatures with an `out` param, which is backward compatible but is a coordinate-system API change worth calling out in the commit message. The one latent risk -- a Float32Array cannot grow if an animation target is longer than the current shape -- is theoretical; I could not construct it through lineAnimationDiff.
